reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical Design - Part 1: General Rules
chapter_title: Annex B (informative): Background information on partial factors for Design Approaches 1, 2 and 3

sections.title: Annex B.1: General
sections.summary: Explains why the three Design Approaches distribute partial factors differently between actions, effects of actions, material properties and resistances: Design Approach 1 requires two separate calculations (Combinations 1 and 2) with factors mostly on actions or on ground parameters (except piles/anchors, factored on resistances); Design Approaches 2 and 3 each need only a single calculation, applying factors to actions/effects of actions and to resistances (DA2) or to structural actions and ground strength parameters (DA3).
sections.body: For limit state types STR and GEO in persistent and transient design situations, three Design Approaches are outlined in 2.4.7.3.4. They differ in the way they distribute partial factors between actions, the effects of actions, material properties, and resistances, in part reflecting differing approaches to allowing for uncertainties in modelling the effects of actions and resistances. In Design Approach 1, checks are in principle required for two sets of factors applied in two separate calculations (Combinations 1 and 2); where it is obvious that one combination governs, the other need not be calculated. Factors are generally applied to actions rather than to the effects of actions, though with one noted exception (2.4.7.3.2(2)). In many cases factors are applied to ground parameters, but for the design of piles and anchors they are applied to resistances. In Design Approaches 2 and 3, a single calculation is required for each part of a design, with the manner of applying the factors varying by the calculation considered: Design Approach 2 applies factors either to actions or to the effects of actions, and to resistances; Design Approach 3 applies factors to actions (or effects of actions) from the structure, and to ground strength (material) parameters.
key_points: Three Design Approaches (2.4.7.3.4) distribute partial factors differently among actions, effects of actions, material properties, and resistances
Design Approach 1: checks are in principle required for two sets of factors in two separate calculations; where one set obviously governs, the other need not be calculated
DA1: factors generally on actions rather than effects of actions (exception 2.4.7.3.2(2)); in many cases on ground parameters, but for piles and anchors on resistances
Design Approach 2: single calculation, factors on actions or effects of actions, and on resistances
Design Approach 3: single calculation, factors on structural actions (or effects of actions) and on ground strength parameters
sections.applicability: Background rationale for choosing among Design Approaches 1, 2, and 3 and understanding how each distributes partial factors.

sections.title: Annex B.2: Factors on actions and the effects of actions
sections.summary: EN 1990:2002 allows the model factor gamma_S;d and the action factor gamma_f to be combined into one factor gamma_F = gamma_S;d * gamma_f multiplying Fk (Eq. B.1); EN 1997-1 uses gamma_F for actions and gamma_E for effects of actions throughout (Annex A Tables A.1, A.3), so national authorities can select alternative values of gamma_S;d x gamma_f. Shows how equations (2.6a)/(2.6b) apply in Design Approach 1 (Eq. B.2), reduce in Design Approach 2 with gamma_M = 1 (Eqs. B.3.1, B.3.2), and remain in their general form in Design Approach 3 (Eqs. B.4.1, B.4.2).
sections.body: (1) EN 1990:2002 states that gamma_f is a partial factor for an action and takes account of the possibility of unfavourable deviations of the action value from its characteristic value; likewise gamma_S;d is a partial factor taking account of uncertainties in modelling the actions and in modelling the effects of actions. (2) EN 1990:2002 allows gamma_S;d and gamma_f to be combined into one factor multiplying Fk: gamma_F = gamma_S;d * gamma_f (Eq. B.1). (3) The various approaches in EN 1997-1 require that factors be applied either to actions or the effects of actions. Since the use of model factors gamma_S;d for actions from the ground will remain exceptional and is therefore left to national determination, gamma_F is used throughout for simplicity for actions and gamma_E for the effects of actions in geotechnical design (see Annex A, Tables A.1 and A.3). This enables national authorities to select alternative values of the combination gamma_S;d x gamma_f. (4) Equations (2.6a) and (2.6b) include Xk/gamma_M in the calculation of actions because ground material properties may affect the values of geotechnical actions in some cases. (5) In Design Approach 1, checks are required for two combinations of sets of factors, applied in two separate calculations. In Combination 1, factors unequal to 1 are generally applied to actions, with factors equal to 1 on the effects of actions: gamma_F != 1 and gamma_E = 1 in equations (2.6a) and (2.6b). An exception is noted in 2.4.7.3.2(2): in cases where it would be physically unreasonable to apply gamma_F != 1 (example: tank with fixed fluid level), then gamma_F = 1 and gamma_E != 1 are used. In Combination 2, gamma_E = 1 is always used, with gamma_F != 1 only for variable actions. Thus, except as noted in 2.4.7.3.2(2), for Design Approach 1 equation (2.6a) applies: Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.2). (6) In Design Approach 2, a single calculation is required for each part of a design, and the way in which the factors are applied either to actions or the effects of actions is varied according to the calculation considered and chosen according to national determination. Either gamma_E != 1 and gamma_F = 1, or gamma_F != 1 and gamma_E = 1 are applied. Since gamma_M = 1 is used, equations (2.6a) and (2.6b) reduce to Ed = gamma_E*E{Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.3.1) or Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.3.2). (7) In Design Approach 3, a single calculation is required; however, a difference is made between actions Frep from the structure and actions from or through the ground calculated from Xk. Either gamma_E != 1 and gamma_F = 1 or gamma_E = 1 and gamma_F != 1 are applied, and equations (2.6a) and (2.6b) remain: Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.4.1) or Ed = gamma_E*E{Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.4.2).
key_points: gamma_F = gamma_S;d * gamma_f (Eq. B.1): EN 1990:2002 allows the model factor and the action factor to be combined into one factor multiplying Fk

EN 1997-1 uses gamma_F for actions and gamma_E for effects of actions throughout (Annex A Tables A.1, A.3); model factors gamma_S;d for actions from the ground remain exceptional, left to national determination
DA1 Combination 1: gamma_F != 1, gamma_E = 1; where gamma_F != 1 is physically unreasonable (e.g. tank with fixed fluid level), gamma_F = 1 and gamma_E != 1 (2.4.7.3.2(2))
DA1 Combination 2: gamma_E = 1 always, gamma_F != 1 only for variable actions; DA1 uses Ed = E{gamma_F Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.2)
DA2: gamma_M = 1; Ed = gamma_E E{Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.3.1) or Ed = E{gamma_F Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.3.2)
DA3: Ed = E{gamma_F Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.4.1) or Ed = gamma_E E{Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.4.2)

equations.description: gamma_F = gamma_S;d * gamma_f: EN 1990:2002 allows the model factor gamma_S;d and the partial factor for an action gamma_f to be combined into one factor multiplying Fk.
Design Approach 1, except as noted in 2.4.7.3.2(2): equation (2.6a) applies, Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.
Design Approach 2 (gamma_M = 1), factor on the effect of actions: Ed = gamma_E*E{Frep; Xk; ad}.
Design Approach 2 (gamma_M = 1), factor on actions: Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad}.
Design Approach 3, factor on actions: Ed = E{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.
Design Approach 3, factor on the effect of actions: Ed = gamma_E*E{Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.

sections.applicability: Understanding how the partial factors on actions and effects of actions are applied differently under each Design Approach's governing equations.

sections.title: Annex B.3: Factors on material strengths and resistances
sections.summary: EN 1990:2002 equation (6.6) and EN 1997-1 equation (2.7c) are equivalent (Eqs. B.5.1, B.5.2); EN 1997-1's gamma_M (on material strengths X) and gamma_R (on resistances R) combine the roles of the material factors gamma_m and resistance model factors gamma_R;d, with the conversion factor eta taken as 1,0. DA1-C1: gamma_M = gamma_R = 1; DA1-C2: gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1 (Eq. B.6.1.1), but for piles and anchors gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1 (Eq. B.6.1.2); DA2: gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1 (Eqs. B.6.2.1, B.6.2.2); DA3: gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1 (Eq. B.6.3.1), sometimes also gamma_R > 1, for example piles in tension (Eq. B.6.3.2).
sections.body: (1) Equation (6.6) of EN 1990:2002 and equation (2.7c) of EN 1997-1 are equivalent: Rd = (1/gamma_R;d)*R{Xi;d; ad} = (1/gamma_R;d)*R{eta_i*Xi;k/gamma_m;i; ad} (EN 1990:2002, equation 6.6; Eq. B.5.1) and Rd = (1/gamma_R)*{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (EN 1997-1, equation 2.7c; Eq. B.5.2). (2) EN 1997-1 equations (2.7a), (2.7b) and (2.7c) include gamma_F*Frep in the calculation of design resistances because the magnitudes of actions may affect the values of geotechnical resistances in some cases, e.g. bearing capacity of a shallow foundation. (3) The value of the conversion factor eta is taken to be 1,0 in EN 1997-1 because the characteristic material strengths are defined to be those relevant to the field situation, thereby including eta in the characteristic value. (4) The various approaches require that factors be applied either to material strengths (X) or to resistances (R); these factors combine the roles of the material factors gamma_m and the resistance model factors gamma_R;d in various ways. For simplicity, the factors applied to material strengths are denoted gamma_M and the factors applied to resistances gamma_R. (5) In Design Approach 1, checks are required for combinations of sets of factors for two separate calculations. In Combination 1, factors equal to 1 are applied to material strength and resistances: gamma_M = gamma_R = 1 in equation (2.7c). In Combination 2, except for piles and anchorages, gamma_M > 1 and gamma_R = 1; thus in most cases Design Approach 1 adopts equation (2.7a): Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.6.1.1). But in Combination 2 for piles and anchors, gamma_M = 1 and gamma_R > 1 are used in equation (2.7b): Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.6.1.2). (6) In Design Approach 2, factors equal to 1 are generally applied to material strengths, with factors greater than 1 applied to resistances: gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1 in equation (2.7b): Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.6.2.1). When gamma_F = 1 is also used, equation (2.7b) takes the form Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.6.2.2). (7) In Design Approach 3, gamma_M > 1 and gamma_R = 1 are generally applied, with equation (2.7a): Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.6.3.1). But sometimes there is also a need to have gamma_R > 1 (piles in tension, for example), so that equation (2.7a) is used as Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}/gamma_R (Eq. B.6.3.2).
key_points: EN 1990 Eq. 6.6 and EN 1997-1 Eq. 2.7c are equivalent (Eqs. B.5.1, B.5.2); gamma_M and gamma_R combine the roles of gamma_m and gamma_R;d; eta = 1,0 (characteristic strengths are those relevant to the field situation)
Eqs. 2.7a/2.7b/2.7c include gamma_F*Frep because the magnitudes of actions may affect geotechnical resistances (e.g. bearing capacity of a shallow foundation)
DA1-C2: gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1, Rd = R{gamma_F Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad} (Eq. B.6.1.1); piles and anchors: gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1, Rd = (1/gamma_R) R{gamma_F Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.6.1.2)
DA2: gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1 (Eq. B.6.2.1); with gamma_F = 1 also, Rd = (1/gamma_R) R{Frep; Xk; ad} (Eq. B.6.2.2)
DA3: gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1 (Eq. B.6.3.1); sometimes also gamma_R > 1 (piles in tension, for example): Rd = R{gamma_F Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}/gamma_R (Eq. B.6.3.2)

equations.description: EN 1997-1 equation 2.7c, equivalent to Eq. B.5.1: Rd = (1/gamma_R)*{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.
Design Approach 1 Combination 2 except for piles and anchorages (gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1, equation 2.7a): Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.
Design Approach 1 Combination 2 for piles and anchors (gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1, equation 2.7b): Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad}.
Design Approach 2 (gamma_M = 1, gamma_R > 1, equation 2.7b): Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk; ad}.
Design Approach 2 when gamma_F = 1 is also used: Rd = (1/gamma_R)*R{Frep; Xk; ad}.
Design Approach 3 (gamma_M > 1, gamma_R = 1, equation 2.7a): Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}.
Design Approach 3 where gamma_R > 1 is also needed (piles in tension, for example): Rd = R{gamma_F*Frep; Xk/gamma_M; ad}/gamma_R.

sections.applicability: Understanding which of the material-strength factor gamma_M or the resistance factor gamma_R governs under each Design Approach, and why.
